title: The robber who became a poet

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever feel like your past is too much to start over? a mistake, a reputation, a version of you you’re not proud of.
options: then this story is yours. listen.
keep them in mind while you hear this one.
good. you might meet someone who needs it.

steps.line: As tradition tells it, a robber named Ratnakara lived in the forest. He stopped travelers and took everything they had, to feed his family.
One day he stopped a wandering sage, Narada, who asked him one quiet question: “Will your family share the weight of what you’re doing?”

steps.q: Ratnakara runs home and asks his family: will you share the weight of what I’ve done? What do they say?
steps.why: They say no. And that answer changes everything.

steps.line: Ratnakara ran home and asked. And they said no. “You chose this. It’s yours.”

steps.q: Why does that answer shake him so badly?
o: He sees the choice was his alone
steps.why: He’d told himself he did it for them. Now he saw the choice, and its weight, were his. That’s where change starts.

steps.line: He came back shaken. Narada gave him a name of God to repeat, and Ratnakara sat down to repeat it.

steps.q: A popular telling says he couldn’t even say the name of Rama at first. So Narada had him say it backwards. What did he repeat?
steps.why: “Mara, mara, mara…” Said over and over, it turns into “Rama, Rama.” He started exactly where he was.

steps.line: He sat so still, for so long, that ants built a hill over him.

steps.q: He sat so still for so long that ants built a hill over him. What does that image say about his change?
o: It happened in a single flash
steps.why: Valmika is Sanskrit for anthill. His new name keeps the slow, still years in it, not just the moment he turned.

steps.line: When he rose, people called him Valmiki, “the one from the anthill.” And Valmiki went on to write the Ramayana.

steps.q: Valmiki doesn’t just write the Ramayana. He walks into it. How?
o: He fights beside Rama at Lanka
He crowns Rama king in Ayodhya
He shelters Sita and raises her sons
steps.why: In the last book, Sita finds refuge in Valmiki’s hermitage, where her twins Lava and Kusha are born. He teaches them his poem, and they sing it before Rama.

say: here’s what i love. the man who gave us the ramayana started out as a robber.
in hindu tradition, who you were isn’t who you have to be. valmiki is the answer to “people don’t change.”

steps.q: Valmiki is called the first poet. Tradition says his first verse burst out when he saw what?
o: A hunter kill one of a pair of birds
Rama leave Ayodhya for the forest
Narada singing the name of Rama
steps.why: Seeing a hunter kill one of two krauncha birds, his grief (shoka) poured out as a new kind of verse, the shloka. The robber who once caused pain was undone by a bird’s.

today.say: think of one thing from your past you’ve let define you. today, do one small thing the new you would do.
options: then do the small thing. that’s how valmiki started too.
that’s honest. sitting still is how he started.
